bull.b: Having an approved, revenue-generating ADC establishes a durable commercial foothold and validates the company’s antibody-drug conjugate platform. ZYNLONTA provides a recurring product revenue base, commercialization experience, and a launch template for label expansions and partnerships that support multi-year growth potential.

A confirmatory Phase 3 efficacy win materially de-risks the clinical program and supports regulatory filings and compendia inclusion. That outcome can unlock broader label access, strengthen commercial uptake, and increase partner interest—structural enablers of sustainable revenue growth and platform credibility.

bull.t: Improved cost discipline and multi-year cash runway
bull.b: Sustained cost reductions and a management-communicated runway through 2028 increase operational resilience, giving the company time to pursue regulatory submissions and commercialization without immediate financing. Durable expense discipline improves margins potential and reduces near-term refinancing urgency.

bear.t: Negative shareholders' equity and rising debt
bear.b: Negative equity and growing debt materially weaken financial flexibility, raising refinancing and covenant risk and limiting strategic options like acquisitions or sizable R&D investment. Over the medium term this structural leverage profile increases the likelihood of dilutive financing or restrictive financing terms.

bear.t: Persistent operating and free cash flow deficits
bear.b: Chronic negative OCF and FCF mean the business remains funding-dependent: continued cash burn constrains reinvestment, forces management to prioritize liquidity over growth, and raises reliance on external capital which can be dilutive and limit long-term strategic flexibility.

bear.t: Safety signals increase regulatory and commercial risk
bear.b: Elevated serious and fatal events in older patients can complicate regulatory review, narrow approved indications, and limit clinician adoption or reimbursement. These safety signals create structural execution risk that may require label restrictions, additional studies, or risk-management measures that reduce market potential.
